subject: SDK onboarding & cutover plan — snippets, timeouts, and rate guidance
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Brody <alex.brody@atlasapps.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SDK onboarding & cutover plan — snippets, timeouts, and rate guidance

Hi Alex — great to meet you last week. As discussed, I've put together an initial runbook for the Atlas Apps cutover from your legacy inference endpoint to Redwood's hosted SDK. High level: SDK install and quickstart, endpoint migration checklist (staged traffic shift), retry/timeout recommendations, and rate-limit safety for peak windows.

Quick asks before we lock in a cutover window:
- Confirm the sandbox API key you want us to test against (if different from the one you shared).
- Preferred maintenance window (we typically recommend a low-traffic 2-hour window; list two options).
- Any compliance constraints (IP allowlist, egress rules) we should factor into the staging run.

Attached: integration-checklist.pdf (action items by party) and a ZIP with SDK snippets and two small code samples that match your Node + Go stacks. Below are the most important runtime knobs we recommend for Atlas Apps based on your latency SLO (~200ms median) and burst traffic pattern: 

Recommended defaults:
- Client timeout: 3,000ms per request
- Connection pool: keepAlive enabled, max sockets 50
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries for idempotent calls (POSTs that are not idempotent should be guarded)
- Rate fencing: client-side token bucket allowing short bursts (500% token refill for 10s) with a sustained limit matching your contract rate.

Example Node snippet (in ZIP) shows how to enable auto-retry + timeout. If you want, Vivek can run a quick smoke test against your sandbox on Thursday. Vanessa will coordinate the cutover checklist on her side.

Next steps:
1) Alex confirms sandbox key + window (reply)
2) We run sandbox smoke test (Vivek)
3) Dry-run cutover with 10% traffic (Vanessa coordinates)
4) Full cutover when metrics look normal (both sides)

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Two quick technical questions from my engineers after reviewing the snippets: 
1) For retries: what is Redwood's recommendation for non-idempotent generation calls where a client-level retry could cause duplicate tokens/credits? Is there a server-side idempotency token support we should use?
2) For timeouts: if we set 3s client-side but the runtime sometimes does prefix caching/writeback that extends the server-side processing to ~4s during cold cache, do you suggest increasing client timeout or changing cache behavior?

Looping in our network ops (nicole@atlasops.com) for allowlisting. Happy to take the smoke test on Thursday.

—Alex

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SDK onboarding & cutover plan — snippets, timeouts, and rate guidance

Alex — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers to your engineers' questions and operational notes (copied for the thread):

1) Retries and idempotency:
- Redwood supports an optional idempotency-token header for generation requests. For non-idempotent calls we recommend adding request-level idempotency tokens at the SDK/agent layer so the server can detect duplicates. The Node sample in redwood-sdk-samples-v2.zip shows how to pass the header: X-Redwood-Idempotency: <uuid-v4>.
- Additionally, set retries=0 for write operations that mutate downstream systems (we can help annotate which endpoints are safe).

2) Timeouts and cache spikes:
- For your scenario (occasional 4s with cold cache), two patterns work well: increase client timeout to 5,000ms, or keep client timeout at 3,000ms but pre-warm model prefixes during the dry-run to minimize cold-starts. Pre-warm will keep user-perceived latency lower but requires a small warmup traffic pattern during the 10% test.
- If you prefer to avoid raising timeouts globally, we can make a short-lived route-level timeout override for the cutover window. Monica can coordinate the route config change and roll it back post-cutover.

Operational items: 
- Nicole (network ops) needs our egress CIDR block; I'll send the list in a separate email to avoid stuffing this thread with large IP lists.
- Vivek: can you take the smoke test on Thu 12/16 02:30 PT if Alex confirms?
- Alex: please confirm the exact cluster (sandbox-atlas-1 vs sandbox-atlas-2) so we point the test to the correct key.

Thanks — I'll prepare a 10% traffic dry-run playbook that includes success metrics (error rate <0.5%, median latency stable within SLA) and a rollback checklist.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference

Great — thank you all for the confirmations. Finalized plan below for clarity (we'll track this in the Drive folder linked above):

Cutover plan (summary)
- Sandbox smoke test: Thu 12/16 02:30 PT (Vivek runs against sandbox-atlas-1 with key sandbox-atlas-2027)
- Dry-run (10%): Sat 12/18 03:00 PT — route 10% traffic, pre-warm prefixes for 30m prior
- Full cutover: target Mon 12/20 02:00–03:00 PT (subject to smoke/dry-run outcomes)

Config decisions
- Client timeout: set to 5,000ms during the dry-run window to avoid transient truncation; rollback to 3,000ms after 48h of healthy metrics
- Retry policy: keep exponential backoff with jitter, max 2 retries for idempotent requests; for non-idempotent flows add X-Redwood-Idempotency header and set SDK retry to 0
- Rate fencing: client token-bucket set to allow 3x burst for 15s and then cap at contracted sustained rate; we'll publish the exact token values in the Drive checklist.

Network ops Nicole — we'll send the egress CIDRs directly to your inbox now. If you need a signed AUP or POA for allowlisting, let us know and Monica will follow up.

Action owners
- Vivek: smoke test + short report (Thu 12/16 morning)
- Vanessa: dry-run playbook + runbook owner for 12/18 dry-run
- Lauren: coordinate go/no-go and client comms
- Alex / Atlas: confirm sandbox cluster and approve the 12/18 dry-run

If there are no objections I'll convert this thread into a single checklist card in the Drive folder and tag owners. Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth cutover.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
